title: French bow versus German bow
summary: American players split about 50-50; he would mix both bows in a symphony section for their different strengths, and himself uses the German bow.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Now, which style of bowing do the jazz musicians generally use French or German?

Oh, either way, you can... There is a... I would say it's a 50-50 proposition in this country. It's about 50% play French bow, 50% play German bow. And I tell you, if I were a conductor in the symphony orchestra, I would try to have a French bow and a German bow divided into each stand, because each bow has a very good advantage. Now, with the French bow, you can play saltellato and spiccato real well. And with the German bow, you can play a good, loud attack, real good, strong notes, you know. So blending the two in a bass section of eight bass players, I think you get a real fine bass section. So I have nothing to say bad against neither the French bow nor the German bow. I think they both have an equal amount of advantage if you put them together.
What do you do, a bow like this and grab it on the end? So that way you've arrived at a compromise? No, I mean, which do you use?
I've been using the German bow. I've been using the German bow.
